feature: Add SSL/TLS Mutual Authentication Between Agent and Server
workflow_rationale: Multi-service security feature requiring implementation across agent-server architecture, PKI infrastructure, deployment artifacts, and development environments. Phases follow service dependency order: shared utilities → server PKI → server HTTPS → agent mTLS → build system → deployment.

phases.name: SSL/TLS Infrastructure (Common)
phases.description: Build shared SSL/TLS utilities and OpenSSL initialization code used by both agent and server

subtasks.description: Create puppet_ssl.h header with OpenSSL data structures and function prototypes

verification.command: test -f include/puppet_ssl.h && grep -q 'puppet_ssl_init' include/puppet_ssl.h

subtasks.notes: Created puppet_ssl.h header file with comprehensive OpenSSL data structures, function prototypes for SSL/TLS operations including initialization, context management, connection handling, and certificate utilities. Follows patterns from puppet_memory.h and config_parser.h. Includes detailed documentation, C++ guards, and OpenSSL 3.0+ EVP API support.

subtasks.description: Create puppet_ssl.c with OpenSSL initialization, cleanup, and certificate loading utilities

verification.command: gcc -c common/puppet_ssl.c -I./include $(pkg-config --cflags openssl) -o /tmp/puppet_ssl.o 2>&1 | grep -v error || echo OK

subtasks.notes: Created puppet_ssl.c with comprehensive OpenSSL utilities. Implemented all functions from puppet_ssl.h including: SSL initialization/cleanup, context management (create/free/configure), certificate/key loading, SSL connection handling (handshake/read/write), certificate verification, and error handling. Follows patterns from puppet_stdlib.c with OpenSSL 3.0+ EVP API compatibility, proper memory management using puppet_malloc/puppet_free, thread-local error buffers, and TLS 1.2+ minimum version support. Note: gcc verification command not available in project, but code follows all specified patterns and implements complete API.

subtasks.notes: Created puppet_ca.h header file with comprehensive CA structures and function prototypes including: CA initialization/cleanup, CA generation/management, CSR signing, certificate storage/retrieval, serial number management, and auto-signing support. Follows patterns from puppet_ssl.h with proper documentation and OpenSSL 3.0+ EVP API compatibility.

subtasks.description: Create puppet_ca.c with CA cert/key generation and CSR signing logic

verification.command: gcc -c server/puppet_ca.c -I./include $(pkg-config --cflags openssl) -o /tmp/puppet_ca.o 2>&1 | grep -v error || echo OK

subtasks.notes: Created server/puppet_ca.c with comprehensive CA implementation including: CA certificate/key generation using EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ compatible), CSR signing with proper X.509 v3 extensions, certificate storage and retrieval, serial number management, and auto-signing stub functions. Implements all functions from puppet_ca.h following patterns from puppet_stdlib.c and puppet_ssl.c. Uses proper memory management (puppet_malloc/puppet_free), secure file permissions (0600 for private keys, 0644 for certificates), thread-local error handling, and proper OpenSSL resource cleanup. Note: gcc verification command not available in project, but code follows all specified patterns and implements complete API. Committed successfully.

subtasks.description: Create puppet_autosign.h and puppet_autosign.c for auto-signing logic

verification.command: gcc -c server/puppet_autosign.c -I./include $(pkg-config --cflags openssl) -o /tmp/puppet_autosign.o 2>&1 | grep -v error || echo OK

subtasks.notes: Created puppet_autosign.h and puppet_autosign.c with comprehensive auto-signing logic implementation. Supports four modes: NONE (manual approval only), NAIVE (auto-sign all for testing), WHITELIST (certname-based with wildcard support), and POLICY (external executable evaluation). Implements configuration file parsing using config_parser API, policy script execution with CSR info via stdin (JSON format), and whitelist file parsing with exact and wildcard pattern matching. Follows patterns from config_parser.c for config parsing, uses puppet_malloc/puppet_free for memory management, includes proper error handling with last_error buffers, and provides complete resource cleanup. Note: gcc verification command not available in project, but code follows all specified patterns and implements complete API.

subtasks.notes:
Successfully refactored puppetc_server.c to support both evhtp (with TLS) and libmicrohttpd (fallback) using conditional compilation. Key changes:
1. Added #ifdef HAVE_EVHTP blocks to support both HTTP libraries
2. Implemented evhtp-based handlers for all endpoints (status, catalog, file_content, file_metadatas, PuppetDB)
3. Integrated puppet_ssl_ctx_t for TLS context initialization using OpenSSL
4. Added CA directory configuration option (-C, --ca-dir)
5. Initialized OpenSSL with puppet_ssl_init() in main()
6. Created SSL context in server mode and passed to evhtp_ssl_init()
7. Maintained backward compatibility with libmicrohttpd (HTTP-only mode)
8. All existing functionality preserved (pluginsync, catalog compilation, PuppetDB queries)
9. Follows patterns from existing code with proper memory management (puppet_malloc/puppet_free)
10. Includes proper error handling and cleanup for SSL resources

The server now supports HTTPS when compiled with HAVE_EVHTP, falling back to HTTP-only with libmicrohttpd. TLS context is initialized but client certificate verification is deferred to subtask-3-4.

subtasks.notes:
Successfully added certificate storage paths and CSR workflow to agent configuration. Changes include:
1. Added DEFAULT_SSL_DIR and DEFAULT_CA_CERT_PATH defines for SSL certificate paths
2. Extended agent_config_t structure with SSL fields: ssl_dir, ssl_cert_path, ssl_key_path, ssl_ca_cert_path

5. Implemented automatic SSL cert/key path building from ssl_dir and certname after certname determination
6. Added verbose logging for SSL configuration paths
7. Paths follow Puppet standard layout:
   - Client cert: /var/lib/puppetc/ssl/certs/<certname>.pem

   - CA cert: /var/lib/puppetc/ssl/ca/ca_crt.pem
8. Verification passed: grep confirms ssl_cert_path present in code

subtasks.description: Implement CSR generation and submission logic in agent

verification.command: grep -q 'X509_REQ\|certificate_request' agent/puppetc_agent.c && echo OK || echo MISSING

subtasks.notes:
Successfully implemented CSR generation and submission logic in agent. Added comprehensive certificate management functions including:
1. generate_private_key() - Generates 2048-bit RSA key using OpenSSL 3.0+ EVP API, saves with 0600 permissions
2. create_certificate_request() - Creates X509_REQ with certname as CN, signs with SHA256
3. csr_to_pem() - Converts CSR to PEM format using BIO memory buffer
4. submit_certificate_request() - POSTs CSR to /puppet-ca/v1/certificate_request/:certname endpoint via libcurl, saves signed cert with 0644 permissions
5. ensure_certificate() - Orchestrates full CSR workflow: checks cert existence, creates directories, generates/loads key, creates and submits CSR

Key implementation details:
- Added OpenSSL headers (ssl.h, x509.h, pem.h, evp.h, bio.h) and sys/stat.h
- Uses EVP_PKEY_CTX API for OpenSSL 3.0+ compatibility (matches pattern from puppet_stdlib.c)
- Follows libcurl patterns from existing request_catalog() function
- Proper memory management with puppet_malloc/puppet_free
- Comprehensive error handling with descriptive messages
- Secure file permissions (0600 for private keys, 0644 for certificates, 0700/0755 for directories)
- Uses existing write_callback() for HTTP response handling

Verification: grep confirms X509_REQ and certificate_request present in code. Committed successfully.

subtasks.description: Configure libcurl with mTLS options (CURLOPT_SSLCERT, CURLOPT_SSLKEY, CURLOPT_CAINFO, verification flags)

subtasks.notes: Configured libcurl with mTLS options in agent. Created configure_mtls_options() helper function that sets CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=1L, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST=2L, CURLOPT_CAINFO, CURLOPT_SSLCERT, and CURLOPT_SSLKEY. Updated submit_certificate_request(), request_catalog(), and check_server_status() to accept agent_config_t* and call configure_mtls_options().
